recovery.body: Mail can be downloaded again from the server, but account settings and unsent messages live only on this device. Quit the app and check that the file above is readable before trying again
recovery.couldNotMove: The files could not be moved. Check that the folder above is writable
recovery.keyNotInTheFile: The key that unlocks the file above is not in the file your master password opens, and this device looks for it nowhere else. The files can be set aside and the app started fresh
recovery.newerBuildBody: The version of Lyonoyl Mail that wrote the file above, or a later one, opens it. Nothing in it has been changed, and this version leaves it as it is
recovery.startFreshMeans: The files that will not open are moved aside — nothing is deleted, and the app names where they went. The app restarts itself with no accounts: add each one again and its mail comes back from the server. Drafts, unsent messages and account settings are not carried over: they stay in the moved files, which the app will not read again
recovery.startFreshMeansKeyring: The files that will not open are moved aside — nothing is deleted, and the app names where they went. The app restarts itself with no accounts: add each one again and its mail comes back from the server. Drafts, unsent messages and account settings are not carried over: they stay in the moved files, which the app will not read again. If {store} still does not answer when the app restarts, the app asks for a master password and keeps your passwords in a file from then on
recovery.theKeyBody: Your mail and settings are whole — the files are untouched and the key is where it has always been, but {store} has not handed it over to this build of the app. Allow access when your system asks, and the app opens by itself. If access was refused, quit the app and open it again
recovery.theKeyringBody: Your mail and settings are whole — the files are untouched, and the key to them is in {store}, which did not hand it over. Start or unlock {store}, then quit and open the app again. If {store} is gone for good, the files can be set aside and the app started fresh
recovery.title: Local storage is unavailable

secrets.chooseBody: This system has no credential store of its own, so there is nowhere to put your mailbox passwords or the key that unlocks your mail. Lyonoyl Mail can keep them in a file on this device instead, readable only with a master password you choose. Nothing is written until you do
secrets.pending: Until this is done, no mailbox can be added or read
secrets.unlockBody: Your mailbox passwords and the key that unlocks your mail are in a file on this device. Enter the master password to open it for this session
secrets.warning: There is no way to recover this password. Without it nothing Lyonoyl Mail keeps on this device can be opened: not the mailbox passwords, not the mail, and not the account settings, drafts and unsent messages that exist nowhere else

settings.needsStorage: Appearance and language are kept in the local database, which could not be opened
settings.noticeShowsHint: Your system draws it, often on a locked screen, and it cannot be taken back once it is shown. Turn off whatever you would rather not have appear there
settings.notificationsHint: Shown only when this window is not the one you are looking at
settings.picturesHint: A picture a message points at lives on somebody else's machine, and fetching one tells that machine your mail was opened just now. “Ask me” leaves a button on each message; “Show them” fetches them as you read. Either way the message never reaches the network itself — the picture is fetched here and handed to it
settings.removeAccountExplains: Its mail, its password and anything waiting to be sent go with it. The mail stays on the server
settings.shareAnonymousDataHint: If something goes wrong, an anonymous report from Lyonoyl Mail helps us fix it sooner. The report never includes your mail, addresses or passwords

settings.storageNotRead: How much is held could not be read
settings.theJournalHint: A record of what happened while it ran — what it fetched, what it refused and why. It never holds an address, a subject or a word of a message, and it is only ever on this device. Send it with a report and the answer takes minutes instead of days
